title: Relative canonical differentials and the comparison of Euler and Picard degrees
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field], [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $C$ be a smooth proper connected curve of dimension one over $k$ [def-sc-curves]. Write $g(C)=\dim_k H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$ [def-sc-genus], let $\Omega_{C/k}$ be the relative differential sheaf of $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf], and write $\omega_C=\Omega^1_{C/k}$ for the canonical sheaf defined from the conormal sheaf of the diagonal [def-sc-kahler-differentials]. There is a canonical isomorphism $\Omega_{C/k}\simeq\omega_C$, agreeing on every affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R$ with the sheaf associated to the module $\Omega_{R/k}$ of Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], and both sheaves are invertible [def-sc-invertible-module]. For every invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module $N$, its Euler-characteristic degree [def-pc-degree-line-bundle], [def-pc-euler-characteristic] agrees with its degree in the Picard group [def-sc-pic0]:
$$\deg_k N:=\chi(C,N)-\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)=\deg_{\mathrm{Pic}}[N].$$
In particular
$$\deg_k\Omega_{C/k}=\deg_k\omega_C=2g(C)-2.$$

source.place: Tag 0C1A (curves-lemma-genus-smooth), canonical differential degree; Tag 0BS6 (curves-lemma-rr), comparison of degree conventions; the relative differential sheaf comparison is morphisms.tex Tag 08S2 (morphisms-lemma-differentials-diagonal).

proof.text: By [lem-sc-diagonal-conormal-derivation-exists], choose the relative derivation into the diagonal conormal with its canonical difference normalization. By [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf], $\Omega_{C/k}$ has affine restrictions associated to $\Omega_{R/k}$ with their universal derivations. Apply [lem-sc-smooth-proper-diagonal-conormal-differentials] to $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$: its relative differential sheaf is precisely this sheaf. The diagonal is closed since $C$ is separated, and its conormal is $\omega_C$ by [def-sc-kahler-differentials]. Inverting the canonical comparison therefore gives $\Omega_{C/k}\simeq\omega_C$, with the asserted affine description. The compatibility of the universal derivations under restriction is part of the cited relative-differential definition.

source.place: Tag 08S2, morphisms-lemma-differentials-diagonal, canonical comparison and its affine description

proof.text: The hypotheses of [lem-sc-canonical-sheaf] hold: $C$ is smooth, connected and of dimension one. Hence $\omega_C$ is locally free of rank one. Restricting the isomorphism of Step 1 to any local trivialization of $\omega_C$ gives a trivialization of $\Omega_{C/k}$, so both sheaves are invertible.

source.place: Tag 02G1, morphisms-lemma-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free, specialized to a smooth curve

proof.text: For any invertible $N$, apply the line-bundle clause of [lem-sc-riemann-roch]: $\chi(C,N)=\deg_{\mathrm{Pic}}[N]+1-g$ and $\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)=1-g$. This clause explicitly uses the Picard/divisor degree of the statement, rather than defining degree by Euler characteristic. Subtraction and [def-pc-degree-line-bundle] give $\deg_kN=(\deg_{\mathrm{Pic}}[N]+1-g)-(1-g)=\deg_{\mathrm{Pic}}[N]$. All hypotheses of the Riemann--Roch node are exactly the present algebraically closed field and proper smooth connected curve.

source.place: Tag 0BS6, curves-lemma-rr; preceding equations equation-degree and equation-degree-c1. The Picard-degree version is supplied by the existing lem-sc-riemann-roch statement.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-canonical-degree] choose a divisor $K_C$ with $\omega_C\cong\mathcal O_C(K_C)$ and $\deg K_C=2g-2$. By [def-sc-pic0], $\deg_{\mathrm{Pic}}[\omega_C]=\deg_{\mathrm{Pic}}[\mathcal O_C(K_C)]=\deg K_C$. Step 3 applied to the invertible $\omega_C$ therefore gives $\deg_k\omega_C=2g-2$. Step 1 makes $\Omega_{C/k}$ and $\omega_C$ the same Picard class, and Step 3 applied to the invertible $\Omega_{C/k}$ gives $\deg_k\Omega_{C/k}=\deg_k\omega_C=2g-2$.
